utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Buenas tardes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Thank you for your perseverance as well.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Oh, no worries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: My name is Jerry Maldonado, and I'm a proud member of the New York Working Families Party and a member of Victoria Ciudadana in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: I'm here to express my support for all four resolutions, all of which revolve around one central question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Who gets to decide a community's future?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: The people who live there or those who profit from its crisis?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Resolutions 27 and 28 get to the heart of the matter, calling for an end to the fiscal control board and the passage of legislation to hold Wall Street hedge funds accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Over the last decade, the Fiscal Control Board's policies have contributed to the closure of more than 400 public schools, the privatization of the island's energy grid, and deep cuts to the island's water infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: The results have been catastrophic, with hundreds of thousands of families like mine suffering from rolling blackouts and water shortages on a regular basis, putting their health and well-being at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: New York City has a moral obligation to act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: As the Bronx burned in the 1970s,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Black and Puerto Rican families bore a disproportionate share of the loss and suffering.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Nearly a quarter million residents were displaced by the politics of austerity led by New York City's own fiscal control board and the closure of firehouses across the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: While we can't undo the damages caused by these policies, the City Council now has an opportunity to right a historic wrong by standing with the people of Puerto Rico and demanding an end to the same failed policies of austerity that cause so much harm and suffering to our communities here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: And as the global epicenter for finance, we must also recognize that debt is another form of colonialism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: A country in debt crisis should not be a bargaining chip for hedge funds like Goldentree to extract outsized profits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: New York's courts should help resolve debt crises, not turn them into profit-making opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Let's pass Resolution 27, calling on the state to close the loophole that rewards predatory hedge funds and debt litigation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: This is the moment to act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: New York must set a standard worthy of our people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: We ask that you support all four resolutions so that we can tax wealth fairly, defend communities from displacement, confront Wall Street greed, and put an end to the control board in defense of democracy, justice, and self-determination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jerry Maldonado
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Jarabel Arroyo, a Puerto Rican in the diaspora, testifies about Project Esencia's threat to Cabo Rojo's environment and communities. She asks the council to pass Resolution 494 to stop the project.
chapters.title: Jarabel Arroyo testifies on Project Esencia

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Buenas tardes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: My name is Yariola Arroyo, and I was born

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: born and raised in Puerto Rico, and I am now part of the diaspora.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: But my heart and hope remains rooted in the island and in the dream of one day returning home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: For us, the question is no longer, will we be able to come home?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: It is, what will be left for us to come back to?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Project Essencia transforms over 2,000 acres

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: of land in Cabo Rojo into a massive luxury tourism and residential complex near environmentally sensitive areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: It raises serious concerns about wetlands and wildlife, water and infrastructure, archaeological sites, public beaches, access, and increased pressure on housing and land.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: And that's not a little thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: And my concern goes beyond Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: If developments of this scale become normalized, if sacrificing our coastline and natural resources for exclusive luxury communities becomes the price of development, where does it stop?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: It's Cabo Rojo today and I'll be another town tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Those of us in the diaspora also have the responsibility to use our voice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: We cannot wave the Puerto Rican flag proudly in New York while remaining silent about the decisions affecting the future of our island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Resolution 494 would put this council on record standing with Puerto Ricans calling for Project Essencia to be stopped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: I support the resolution and ask this council to pass it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Because it's

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: It is bigger than this development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: It is whether Puerto Rico will continue to be a place where Puerto Ricans themselves can live, return, and belong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Puerto Rico is our home, and I refuse to accept a future where our people can only afford to remember it as a future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Can only remember it from afar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Despierta, boricua, que no robar lo nuestro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jarabel Arroyo
utterances.text: Esencia no va.

chapters.summary: David Galarza Santa, a Puerto Rican New Yorker, testifies in support of Resolutions 27, 28, 494, and 372. He emphasizes that New York City has a responsibility to act because many financial institutions involved are based there.
chapters.title: David Galarza Santa testifies on resolutions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Madeline Jackson
utterances.text: You hear me?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Madeline Jackson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairwoman and the members of the committee, and a special thanks to Councilmember Alex Aviles for introducing these historic resolutions that will hopefully be replicated in cities across the United States that have significant and really vital Puerto Rican communities as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: My name is David Galalza Santa, and I am a Puerto Rican New Yorker and a member of the Puerto Rican diaspora.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: We stand here, or sit actually in this case, at the Schomburg Center, named for Arturo Alfonso Schomburg, an Afro-Boricua who came to New York and helped organize Puerto Rican and Cuban independence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: His legacy reminds us that the diaspora has always been a part of the struggle for Puerto Rico's freedom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: We're not spectators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: We are part of that struggle, and we follow the leadership of the people in Puerto Rico, which is why I'm glad that there were so many on the Zooms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: That is why we demand the passage of Resolutions 27, 28, 494, and 372.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Resolution 27 would stop Wall Street from profiting Puerto Rico's debt crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: New York is not a bystander.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Our laws and our financial institutions play a direct role in Puerto Rico's debt crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: If Wall Street profits from Puerto Rico, New York City has a responsibility to act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Resolution 28, end La Junta.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Over 3 million Puerto Ricans cannot be governed by an unelected fiscal board that imposes austerity and puts creditors before people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico deserves self-determination, not financial occupation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Resolution 494, stop Project Esencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Cabo Rojo is not a playground, nor Puerto Rico is a playground for billionaires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Our land, water, and equal systems are not commodities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: For luxury development, Puerto Rico is not for sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: The City Council's own resolution documents the project's scale, its potential environmental impacts, and the New York-based organizing against it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Resolution 372, repeal Act 22, Act 60.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico must not become a tax shelter for millionaires and billionaires while working class Boricuas face displacement, unaffordable housing, and rising costs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: And this is precisely why New York City must speak up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Many of the corporations, financial institutions, developers, and other interests that make decisions affecting more than 3 million Boricuas are based here or operate here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: JPMorgan Chase, The Mandarin, Amman, and Rosewood Hotels, and the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Time expires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: The decisions may be made in borders of my hand, but Puerto Rico is living in, they live the consequences in San Juan, Cabo Rojo, Vieques, Loiza, Ponce, communities across the archipelago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: So we're saying, in New York, use your power to stand with Puerto Rico, not to profit, not to profit from Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Our land, our water, our resources, our future is not a commodity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico is not for sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico is not a tax haven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico is not a colony to be managed for profit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: And we demand the passage, the passage resolutions 27, 28, 494, and 372.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: And we will continue to organize here in New York and across the diaspora until Puerto Rico has justice, self-determination, and freedom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Galarza Santa
utterances.text: Puerto Rico no se vende, esencia no va, se acabaron las corazas, que viva Puerto Rico libre.

chapters.summary: Gabriel Fantacone, deputy director at Churches United for Fair Housing, testifies in support of Resolution 27 and the Champerty Bill. He explains how vulture funds profit from distressed sovereign debt and calls for its repeal.
chapters.title: Gabriel Fantacone testifies on Champerty Bill

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Hello?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Is this on?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Thank you to Madam Deputy Speaker, Councilmember Aviles, the Cultural Affairs Committee, and the Broad Coalition standing with us today, fighting for the dignity of Puerto Rico and its citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: My name is Gabriel Fantacone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: I'm Deputy Director of Civic Engagement and Research at Churches United for Fair Housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: I'm here today urging immediate adoption of all of the aforementioned resolutions, but particularly Resolution 27 by the City Council, which calls for the immediate passage of the Champerty Bill,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Assembly Bill A643A, by the New York State Assembly upon the opening of the 2027 legislative session.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: The Champerty Bill repeals a decades-old carve-out that allows a group of Wall Street vulture funds to profit off of debt-distressed countries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: These funds make a living of buying distressed sovereign debt bonds and immediately suing for full repayment plus interest in New York State courts, driving these nations into deeper fiscal crisis and profiteering the suffering of entire peoples.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: This type of litigation is permissible for sovereign debt bonds due to a deliberate carve-out in state law passed by the vulture funds 20 years ago that has devastated Puerto Rico and so many other nations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Champers litigation is one of the direct causes of Puerto Rico's debt crisis in the 2010s, and the Vulture Fund's behavior and profit model was directly responsible for the years of economic devastation and forced migration that followed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Sadly, Puerto Rico is one of many nations that have been targeted under this carve-out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: with countries such as Argentina losing $2.4 billion to the vulture funds, all while facing deep socioeconomic devastation as a result.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: For New Yorkers such as myself who come from and represent immigrant communities forced to leave their homes due to economic exploitation, this legislation isn't just important, it's personal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: We have an opportunity to change our state financial policy for the better and to advance global economic justice from inside the halls of the state capitol.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the City Council for advancing and considering Reso 27, calling on the Assembly to pass the Champerty Bill for the benefit of Puerto Rico and all nations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: I'm using the word nation here because we support Puerto Rican independence in this house.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: And I ask the city council, and I'm also grateful to my partners on the Debt Justice Alliance and to Assemblymember Jessica Gonzalez-Rojas, who couldn't be here today, but whose presence is felt through her fierce sponsorship of the Champerty Bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: I ask the city council and the assembly, please stand on the right side of history and help us pass these historic pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gabriel Fantacone
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams announces that the committee must leave the space in an hour and apologizes in advance if they have to enforce time limits strictly.
chapters.title: Chair Williams announces time limit

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I just want to make a quick announcement that we have to leave this space in an hour.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And so this is a proactive apology if we have to really enforce the time.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I try my hardest not to, but we're in the field.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And so we have to act as guests.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We're not in the council.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: So at City Hall, I just want to say that in advance, our apologies.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We know this is very important and we thank you so much for your testimony, but

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We may need to start.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: If not, we have to start enforcing the time.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Alicia Nascimento, political director at New York Communities for Change, testifies in support of Resolution 27. She explains the history of the Champerty loophole and how it allows vulture funds to profit from debt-distressed countries.
chapters.title: Alicia Nascimento testifies on Champerty loophole

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Good afternoon and thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the broader committee and especially to Councilmember Alexa Aviles for introducing these historic resolutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: My name is Alicia Nascimento.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: I am the political director at New York Communities for Change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: In 2006, when Puerto Rico's debt crisis was unraveling, our Puerto Rican members watched their homeland being squeezed by a crisis that had nothing to do with their creation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Schools and hospitals were closing, people were losing their pensions, and they asked us, what can we do from New York?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: At the time, we didn't think we could do much, but it turns out that as the financial capital of the world, there is a lot that we can do, and that is within our power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Puerto Rico may be nearly 2,000 miles away, but the laws governing its debt can be written right here because about half of the world's sovereign debt is actually governed by New York state law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Champerty is an old English law that has been in the books in New York since the early 1800s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: It was actually meant to stop people from buying someone else's debt just to sue them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: But in 2004, a loophole was created by a billionaire hedge fund investor named Paul Singer, who, as Gabe himself has described, has pillaged Argentina,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: took Argentina on a 15-year litigation battle using our courts to ultimately...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: extract about $2 billion while Argentinians themselves were undergoing a severe economic crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: This is what happens when Wall Street gets to write the rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Vulture funds get richer and ordinary people pay the price.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: It's the same things that we've been seeing happening in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: And that's exactly why we're fighting to close the Champerty loophole and why we're supportive of all the resolutions, but particularly Resolution 27.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: We're not saying that investors can't invest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: We understand that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: But we're saying that you shouldn't be able to buy a country's debt for pennies on the dollars, refuse to negotiate, and then use our courts to demand the full amount at the expense of our people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: This is why NYCC and the Debt Justice Alliance alongside our partners, Cuff, Strong Economy for All, Center for Popular Democracy, urged to pass Resolution 27 and to stand with us in Albany.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: And I just wanted to close with saying that our court should be a place for justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: It's not a place where vulture funds can extract as much money as possible from countries and hold them hostage, which is what we've been doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: So let's get this done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia Nascimento
utterances.text: Thank you all.

chapters.summary: Jorge Lopez Martinez, on behalf of the Defiende a Cabo Rojo Coalition, testifies in support of Resolutions 494 and 28. He describes Project Esencia as a neocolonial settlement that would steal water and destroy ecosystems.
chapters.title: Jorge Lopez Martinez testifies on Defiende a Cabo Rojo

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: My name is Jorge Lopez Martinez, and I'm here on behalf of the Defiende a Cabo Rojo Coalition, La Coalición Defiende a Cabo Rojo, to address the Council Committee in support of Resolution 494 and Resolution 28.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: At Defiende a Cabo Rojo, a broad coalition of individuals and organizations based in southwestern Puerto Rico, with allies across the archipelago and the diaspora, like myself,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: We have taken on the duty of defending and protecting our people, land, water, and heritage against the present pattern of dispossession and destruction disguised as investment and development and facilitated by a racist, neocolonial, pro-billionaire political economy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: The private city Essencia proposed for construction in Cabo Rojo further restricts the right to self-determination and territorial sovereignty that Puerto Rico lacks as a U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Colony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Greenwashed in its marketing, Essencia is a neocolonial settlement and enclave for billionaires promoted by foreign firms like the Rubin Brothers and local ones like Three Rules Capital with the complicity of the colonial government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: As other mega projects looming over us like Moncayo, The Cliff, Loiza Ocean, among others, Essencia would not benefit the Puerto Rican economy at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Yet the government has already given them over $500 million in tax exemptions and credits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: This same government is now advancing unconstitutional laws and amendments to favor oligarchs and technocrats, dismantling

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: environmental protections, and give projects like this free rhyme.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Sounds familiar?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: All of this overlooked by an undemocratic, aimless, U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Congress-imposed fiscal oversight board known as La Junta that over the past 10 years has spent over more than $2.2 billion from the already constrained government budget.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: To our people,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Essencia would offer just a handful of jobs in service of the same ultra-rich, white class responsible for 50% of global carbon emissions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Like other cases in Mexico, Hawaii, Jamaica, and the one halted by the Albanian people, Essencia recreates the extractivist plantation economy and enslavement of a not-so-distant past in the Caribbean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Essencia would also steal millions of gallons of water on a daily basis in an area suffering from chronic shortages and characterized by its dry climate conditions,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: destroy ecosystems like mangroves and coastal lagoons shielding us from the climate crisis in a zone of protected ecologically valuable soils and adjacent wildlife reserves,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: fragment a coastal subtropical dry forest biodiversity hotspot and home to the endemic and endangered species, desecrate archaeological sites and monetize our indigenous heritage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Privatize one of the few remaining pristine beaches left in Puerto Rico, tear apart the social fabric of the community characterized by working class.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you try to wrap it up in 30 seconds, please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Yes, this is important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Fishing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: LGBTQ plus and Afro-Puerto Rican traditions as well as by a local tourist economy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Displace our population and replace it with elites who believe themselves to be owners and masters of everything and everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Despite 534 years of colonization, Boricay has always been, is, and will be free in our consciousness and action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: We belong to our beloved islands and its proud heritage of struggle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Puerto Ricans living here in New York like myself know what it's like to be displaced from our homeland.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: We are determined to not allow it anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Whatever it takes, Esencia will not be built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Esencia no va.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: We will not be erased.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: This struggle is for our lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jorge Lopez Martinez
utterances.text: Y a la junta ni un vaso de agua.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams thanks the panel and calls the next panel. Nduja Nitri, of Victory in Puerto Rico, testifies about the impact of La Junta and the importance of supporting the resolutions to preserve Puerto Rican culture and land.
chapters.title: Chair thanks and calls next panel; Nduja Nitri testifies

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Okay, thank you guys so much for testifying.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: You don't have anything?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Madeline Jackson
utterances.text: No, because we don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Okay, yes, so the next panel, Calaris, Erica, Ramon Cruz, Jose Laluc, Power Malou, and Nduja Nitri.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Did I say that right?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Nitri?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Anduja.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: No, that's fine, but what is it?

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I might have to step out for a second for a call, but I'm sure Councilmember slash my co-chair for today, you are the co-chair of today, Alexa Aviles will facilitate.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Induja, do your thing.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Oh, I'm starting.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Yes, I think the council member said you.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Oh, I was last.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Do your thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Hola a todos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: My name is Nduja Netri, third in command of Victory in Puerto Rico, a grassroots organization committed to defending our land, our communities, and reclaiming our culture, both in the diaspora and on the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: As a second-generation Nuyorican, I spent most of my life in an identity crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Not Puerto Rican enough and definitely not American.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Only to learn and recognize that it's systematically designed this way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Oppression, division, and assimilation in the states, on the island, and everywhere between the two.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Stateside, it comes in the form of gentrification in thriving Puerto Rican neighborhoods and communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: On the island, our motherland, a slow genocide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Because of the illegal debt under La Junta, hundreds of thousands are...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: affected by constant water and electrical outages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Even worse, the closing of hospitals and schools across the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Just three decades ago, we had the Young Lords Party here in New York City taking over Lenox Hill Hospital, and as a result, we now have Medicaid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Learning from and with the help of the Black Panthers Party created a free breakfast program in El Barrio.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: We must take pause and realize that we, Boricuas across the diaspora, are still fighting for our human basic rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: This imperialist nation wants us dumb or dead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Thus, they are illegally trying to speed up the process for final stages of this cultural and national genocide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Unless we choose to do something now, from every and any angle, Resolutions 27, 28, and 494, proposed by Councilwoman Alexa Aviles, and support for these resolutions is an important step in preserving our birthright,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: our history, our culture, and our legacy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: This is just one way of defending what is rightfully ours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: What happens there happens here and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: My great-grandparents'land was taken to build the Ramay Air Force Base in Aguadilla, and while I cannot return to their birthplace, I can still...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: still return to their graves and the sacred lands they walked, a privilege and honor they want to strip away, a birthright being threatened as I speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: We have a responsibility to look back and as an homage to those before us, use this privilege to protect Borinquen and Boricuas worldwide, to build and bridge gaps in knowledge, community, and service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Grateful to everyone in this fight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Porque el pueblo sabe el pueblo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Esencia no va.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nduja Nitri
utterances.text: Y que viva Puerto Rico libre.

chapters.summary: An unnamed speaker testifies about Project Esencia's threat to Cabo Rojo, citing scientific studies and the project's potential for ecocide. They criticize the governor's visit to Wall Street and call for passing the resolutions.
chapters.title: Unnamed speaker testifies on Project Esencia

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This is a historic hearing at the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Arturo Schomburg fought for the independence of Puerto Rico, coined the term Afro-Borinqueno, and was born in my dad's birthplace of Santurce, Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you to Councilmember Aviles and all of our comrades in this City Council for putting Puerto Rico at the forefront with Resolutions 494, 27, 28.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: From New York to El Moro, no a Proyecto Esencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Ojo en Cabo Rojo, esto es nuestra herencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Is our home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And Proyecto Esencia in Cabo Rojo is a detriment to our people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Proyecto Esencia is being proposed to open the floodgates of displacement and get the developers closer to having a Puerto Rico without Puerto Ricans and no coquise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: They want the cage, not the birds, so they spray the trees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The government of Puerto Rico expects the people to be okay with the fast tracking of permits for luxury projects before proper testing is complete to ensure the project will be safe for flora, fauna, and human life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This basically translates to shoot first, ask questions later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: That is reckless and irresponsible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: By then, it will be too late and irreversible damage will already have taken place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The scientific community of Puerto Rico volunteered their time to study, analyze, and break down Proyecto Esencia and why it is not a go and an all-the-way no.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: 44 professionals in Puerto Rico, including ecologists and other experts dedicated to the environment and the study of biodiversity, have determined that this project will have an irreversible negative impact on the ecosystem and will

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: result in an ecocide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: June 30th, 2026 marked 10 years after Promesa and La Junta de Control Fiscal were imposed on Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And on August 25th, two months later, the governor of Puerto Rico decided to visit Wall Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Stock exchange to ring the opening bell and yell that Puerto Rico is open for business and for sale.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You cannot make up the irony because La Junta de Control Fiscal sided with the Wall Street vultures that preyed on Puerto Rico's debt, buying distressed bonds for pennies on the dot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: and positioning themselves to profit from an island and financial collapse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Wall Street rushed with vulture funds aiming to take flight, swooping down on their prey with no oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Crisis after crisis, the people are told to sacrifice, while outside investment and luxury development are invited in under the guise of bringing progress and prosperity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: With all these investors making deals for luxury developments, the people still suffer a significant high level of social and economic inequality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: 39% of Puerto Ricans live below the poverty line, and according to Puerto Rico Family Data Center, more than 52% of children living in poverty conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: That's more than four times the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: National child poverty average.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So who is this progress actually for?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: While financial institutions talk about investment, capital, and economic opportunity, Puerto Ricans and Puerto Rico

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: have lived through austerity, an unreliable electric grid, water shortages, rising costs, displacement, and the privatization of essential services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Luxury resorts are not needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: What the people need is access to clean water, health care, education, affordable housing, and lower food costs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: New York City is the belly of the corporate beast, taking advantage of Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Passing all three resolutions will demonstrate that Puerto Rico is not alone in this fight, and we will continue taking steps to end the oppression.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Abuse, once and for all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: No a Proyecto Esencia.

chapters.summary: Jose La Luz, a lifelong labor organizer, testifies about the need to end the fiscal control board. He argues the board has failed to restore economic growth and has imposed draconian austerity measures.
chapters.title: Jose La Luz testifies on ending La Junta

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: My name is Jose La Luz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: I'm a lifelong labor organizer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: I was one of the leaders of the multi-union coalition that achieved collective bargaining rights for 120,000 public workers in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: I want to offer three compelling reasons to end the fiscal control board, or as we call it, La Junta in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: And I echo most, if not all, of what has been said throughout the entire morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: The board has failed to restore the essential conditions for economic growth and recovery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: And that's very serious.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: It has prevented the massive investment that rebuilding of the infrastructure for the electrical grid and water supply requires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: And the draconian austerity measures, it has imposed exacerbated existing wealth and income inequality, which have taken an enormous toll

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: on working families throughout the archipelago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: Its actions have fostered the privatization of essential public utilities and public services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: imposing a burden on the rapidly declining standard of living for working families and the middle class, while incomes and wages have remained stagnant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: Its very existence, that is the existence of La Junta, has prevented

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: fundamentally the development of a lasting solution to the economic and financial crisis which will require

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: a political alternative predicated on the exercise of self-determination and putting an end to colonialism in accordance with international law under the supervision of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose La Luz
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the opportunity to testify.

chapters.summary: Dr. Kaliris Salas-Ramirez testifies about her family's history of public service in Puerto Rico and the impact of austerity measures. She calls for approving the resolutions to end colonization and austerity.
chapters.title: Kaliris Salas-Ramirez testifies on austerity

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Okay, this is working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My name is Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Kaliri Salas Ramirez, pronouns she, her, ella, daughter of Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Salvador Salas and Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Doris Ramirez, both professors at the University of Puerto Rico, Mayagüez campus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I was born, raised, and educated on the island of Puerto Rico and came to New York City in December of 2007 and have devoted the last 16 years of my life

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: to racial and educational equity here in the most segregated education system in the country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I do that because I lived on an island that was consistently told to come to America to live the dream.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I lived on an island where we all had to work really hard, and my sister devoted 23 years of her life to the public electrical company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Every single person in my family has devoted their blood, sweat, and tears to education in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My cousin being a special education teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My aunt devoting her life to Head Start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My other aunt devoting her life to being a high school counselor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My uncle being the mayor of San Sebastian, Puerto Rico, El Honorable Silverio Lello Salas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: My father, as Secretary of Natural Resources of the island of Puerto Rico, truly the first academician to be a political...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: in Puerto Rico as Secretary of Natural Resources under Sila Calderón.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: We have for a long time, the Salas family, has devoted their life to public service of Puerto Rico because of the austerity measures that exist in the corrupt

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: government that has been consistently perpetuating white supremacy on the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: We have consistently have to be without allowing people like Julia Callagher to come and close half of our public schools in Puerto Rico and in turn allowing for charter schools to come and privatize public education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Allowing the fiscal control board to close multiple...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Resources towards the university system that has allowed my family to move in social mobility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: And so I wanted to come here today to be really personal about this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Nobody was planning to stay here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: I was funded by the University of Puerto Rico to get my doctorate and come back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: To serve as an educator, and I have not been able to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: In order to be able to move our island forward, these resolutions have to be approved, and we must stand with our fellow Puerto Ricans, and we must end these austerity measures and this colonization that we are existing in,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: both on the island and here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kaliris Y. Salas-Ramirez
utterances.text: Que viva Puerto Rico libre.

chapters.summary: Ramon Cruz, external affairs coordinator for Movimiento Victoria Ciudadana, testifies in support of the four resolutions. He asks who decides how Puerto Rico's resources are used and who benefits from those decisions.
chapters.title: Ramon Cruz testifies on resolutions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Okay, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: My name is Ramon Cruz, and I'm the External Affairs Coordinator for the Movimiento Victoria Ciudadana, a movement committed to a progressive and anti-colonial vision for Puerto Rico and to building a more transparent, equitable, and socially responsible government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Today I want to address you in favor of your four resolutions, the Fiscal Control Board, Act 22, and Essencia Project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: These are all connected by one fundamental question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Who decides how Puerto Rico's resources are used?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Who benefits from those decisions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: And who ultimately bears the costs?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Ten years after Promesa, Victoria Ciudadana believes the Fiscal Control Board must go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Puerto Rico cannot speak of true democracy while fundamental decisions over our public resources remain subject to an entity imposed upon rather than elected by the Puerto Rican people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: For years, Puerto Ricans have been told that fiscal responsibility requires sacrifice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: But fiscal responsibility cannot mean austerity for workers and communities while tax incentives, government contracts, and benefits to powerful economic interests escape the same scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: That principle applies to Act 22.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: We support investment and we welcome people who want to make Puerto Rico their home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: But when government provides extraordinary tax advantage,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: It must demonstrate the public benefits with data on jobs, wages, revenues, and economic returns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: And we must examine also the effects of housing and displacement when families earning local wages compete in an increasingly unaffordable market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: So this is not what Act 22 has left us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: And Act 22 doesn't help Puerto Ricans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: The same principles applies to Essencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: We're not against development, but recent Puerto Rican Senate hearings have raised serious questions about water, infrastructure, environmental impacts, and costs to surrounding community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: And development must demonstrate a genuine public benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: But this is not what Essencia does.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: So far, what these three issues point out is that Puerto Rico is for the wealthy that have no interest in the development of our people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: That is why we condemn all of this and support your resolution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Ultimately, our standards should be simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Does our economic model allow the people who work in Puerto Rico to afford a home, raise their families, and build their future there?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: So Puerto Rico's resources must serve Puerto Rico's people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ramon Cruz
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Staff calls the next panel. Alberto Urbina, co-founder of Daughters and Sons of Borinquen, testifies in support of all four resolutions, criticizing Wall Street's predatory practices and the Essencia project.
chapters.title: Council Staff calls next panel; Alberto Urbina testifies

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next, we're going to thank you so much to the panel.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next, we're going to have Angel Garcia.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Alberto Urbiño, Yvette Aguirre, Olga Zanabria, and Alan Aja.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Helen Colon, are you here?

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Alberto, would you like to start?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Yeah, no problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilwoman Naviles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: It's a pleasure to be here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: My name is Alberto Urbina.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: I am the co-founder of Daughters and Sons of Borinquen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: And this is in regards to Resolution 27, this particular remark.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: I was born and raised in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: I was born in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: So I'm fully aware of the predatory practices Wall Street uses on U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Soil.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: So what would make me think that they would not weaponize debt against a colony that they have extorted, monopolized, and terrorized since 1898?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: We are not indebted to you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Our blood, our resources, our culture, our military service, and our land is why this country is indebted to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Daughters and Sons of Boarding King supports Resolution 27.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: In regards to Resolution 28, we must end La Junta.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: I mean, I think this is obvious, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: This is the epitome of colonialism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: We have absolutely no say in the financial dealings of our beloved boarding king.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: We defer to a corrupt and vicious board that has absolutely no interest in the rebuilding of...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: infrastructure or the upliftment of the people of Borinquen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: They simply want a Borinquen without Borinquas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Daughters and Sons supports Resolution 28.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: As far as Act 22,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Now under Act 60, which continues to move the goalposts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Act 22 now operating under Act 60 has, because of Law 38, extended this egregious program to new investors through 2055, which is insane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: And I mean, we can talk about a thousand things that are wrong with this, but I only have two minutes, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: We don't want to have that problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: So we may not be able to fight future investors through legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: In addition, we remain deeply concerned that those who are grandfathered in will continue to benefit retroactively from the recolonization construct, a system that is shameful

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: but certainly not foreign, coming from a country that has built its status on the flesh of those that it detests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: We support Resolution 372.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Resolution 494, stop the Essencia project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: The incredibly grotesque Essencia project is looking to destroy approximately 2,000 acres of coastal land in Cabo Rojo

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: without a thought for the fracturing of the bio-communities that will experience irreversible effects so the elite can play golf and watch the sunset from their multi-million dollar condos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Boricuas who spent generations building culture through love and community are displaced and ultimately erased.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: To that we say, Esencia Nova.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Que viva Palestina libre, Congo libre, Yemen libre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Cuba libre y todos los pueblos que sufren en la lucha contra la opresión libre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Daughters and sons of Orinquin, a la orden.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: And Nolan Wells, say his name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alberto Urbina
utterances.text: Nolan Wells, say his name.

chapters.summary: Yvette Aguirre testifies about her experience owning a condominium in Puerto Rico and seeing Puerto Ricans bought out by investors. She supports the resolutions, particularly Resolution 372 to repeal Act 22.
chapters.title: Yvette Aguirre testifies on tax haven

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: So I'm in favor of passing all the resolutions, particularly the 372.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And I just want to speak from my own experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: I was born in Puerto Rico, and I own a condominium in Puerto Rico on the waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And when I bought 30 years ago, everybody in the building were Puerto Ricans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And now you can count the Puerto Ricans in one hand.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: You have to state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: You can't...

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: State your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Oh, my name is Ivera Aguirre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Ivera Aguirre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And now my building is filled with all investors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And we're all waterfront.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: The prices have gone up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: The Puerto Ricans have bought out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: We're all bought out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And it's a tax haven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: What they're doing is they're buying for the purpose of we can deduct my expenses in Puerto Rico on my U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Taxes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Because it's an investment property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: That has taught me, by good accountants, that you can deduct your trips, your food, your taxes, your electricity, your cable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: You can deduct everything by living part-time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: All you have to do is...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: do is step into the island twice a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And not even for any amount of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: You just get off the plane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: A lot of them, you get off the plane, I see them for one day, and then I never see them again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And so that's what has happened in my area in Isla Verde.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: All of them are being bought out by these American, USA investors because it's a tax haven.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Yvette Aguirre
utterances.text: And so that is, I think, the reason why they want to keep investing in Puerto Rico and why they want to keep giving up all of our land, because they are controlling the whole system.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Angel Garcia, a resident of the South Bronx born in Cabo Rojo, testifies in support of all resolutions. He focuses on Resolution 494 and calls on the City Council to investigate JPMorgan Chase's role in funding the project.
chapters.title: Angel Garcia testifies on Project Esencia

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: It's also called settler colonialism is what that is.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Siguiente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: Hi, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: My name is Angel Garcia, and I'm a resident of the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: First, I want to speak in support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: I want to make sure that it's clear that I give full support to all four resolutions under consideration by the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: I want to focus a couple of my points today on Resolution 494 concerning the Essencia project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: And I'll speak first from a personal perspective, like my colleague here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: I was born in Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: And I've gone back there a number of times over the years and have several family households and homes scattered throughout Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: That is, uncles and aunts living in different homes there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: That's their homeland.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: Speaking of home, I'm also a co-heir to a house in Cabo Rojo, which my brothers and I hope to sell at some affordable price to a working class Puerto Rican family

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: that will make it their long-term home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: The point is that we are heirs because my mother and father achieved a dream that's common to many Puerto Ricans who migrated to the United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: Get a job, work, and save enough to buy a house in Puerto Rico where they could retire and live in peace in the homeland.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: and they were able to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: Puerto Rico must continue to be a homeland where the homes are affordable to those here in New York City

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: and elsewhere in the United States who want to return and make their life there, and to those in the motherland who are renting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: And want permanent, long-term home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: The other point I'll make here is, in addition to supporting the resolutions that the council has considered today, is to consider taking action regarding JPMorgan Chase,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: the key funder in the $2.3 billion luxury project for homes ranging from $2 million to $20 million.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: In current prices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: The City Council should seriously investigate the possibility of suspending or terminating the City Government's financial relationships, both banking and pension fund investments,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: with Chase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: This is a funder of environmental destruction and the deprivation of water and power from a people suffering through waves of blackouts and power outages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: As well as drought conditions recently declared disasters by the United States and the island government just last month.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Angel Garcia
utterances.text: Again, I speak in support of all the resolutions today, and thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Alan Aja, chair of the Department of Puerto Rican and Latinx Studies at Brooklyn College, testifies about the historical context of the resolutions. He calls for massive reparations and political and economic sovereignty for Puerto Rico.
chapters.title: Alan Aja testifies on Puerto Rican studies

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Muchisimas gracias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Thank you, colega.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: I want to thank Councilmember Aviles for your immense work today as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: My name is Alan Aja.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: I'm the chair and professor in the Department of Puerto Rican and Latinx Studies at Brooklyn College.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: This is a department founded over 50 years ago through student activism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Let's go.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Students who, in their struggle for curricular inclusion at CUNY, connected the anti-colonial struggles of the Puerto Rican people through their practice here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: It is indeed appropriate that this hearing is being held at the Schomburg Center, hence the self-described Afro-Borinqueno abolitionist historian.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: There's a really fun fact about Schomburg is that he would sometimes use the pseudonym Guadionex in editorials he published in the New York Times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Guadionex, of course, is the indigenous or Taino cacique who resisted Spanish colonialism on Quisqueya, now Haiti in the DR.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Clearly, 400 years later, Schomburg was honoring his legacy, writing not just with eyes on Puerto Rican and Cuban independence, but at a time of burgeoning U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Colonialism in the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: One of the ironies and the appalling effects of the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Colonial project in Puerto Rico is that over a century of extraction of Puerto Rican labor, land, and culture is the notion that the country is required to pay back debts?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Where have we heard this before?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: We know that Ley 22, La Junta, Project Esencia, to the very luma that Bad Bunny eviscerated through song and protest at the Super Bowl, they aren't new.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: They are the present manifestations of an ugly history of imposed U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Policy of leyes and plans and operaciones that exploit workers, extract resources, poison the water, and displace the people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: When La Junta was conceived, the people saw the debt trap that was coming, a boon for bondholders and private equity, while public sector, the hospitals, the schools, electricity experiences austerity, the subvestment of privatization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Including pensions that are taxed in order to pay back these so-called debts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: In reality, if anyone owes a debt, it's those who set the trap.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: The least we can do is pass these resolutions, acting in solidarity with our neighbors that we heard online.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: I must highlight the racist audacity of the dual occupation of Cabo Rojo, as has been shared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: A recent study by Camila Rodriguez Tolento questions if it is not esencia, but ausencia.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Or in existence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: The researcher, along with many scientists and activists, are warning us of the impact of the carbon footprint in the era.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: We've heard it all today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Shame on you, J.P.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Morgan Chase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: As we support the bare minimum through these resolutions, we must be in solidarity with our friends in Puerto Rico, we heard in testimonies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: After Hurricane Maria,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Activists and scholars called for a quasi-martial plan, an obligation of the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: To rebuild the infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Instead, it got more austerity, more extraction, more exploitation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: It's clear we need something more radical that channels the spirit of Guadionex.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: This is a call for massive reparations, island-wide to household level, support for food, energy, and a political and economic sovereignty that is free of the reigns of U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Imperialism.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alan Aja
utterances.text: Palante.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Palante.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Gracias.

chapters.summary: Helen Colon, from El Puente, testifies about the organization's analysis of Project Esencia's environmental impacts. She supports all four resolutions and highlights the project's threat to vulnerable species and habitats.
chapters.title: Helen Colon testifies on El Puente and Esencia
