utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Good afternoon, buenas tardes a todos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: My name is Helen Colon, and I am a proud Boricua, born in Puerto Rico, raised in New York, Brooklyn, and I work for an amazing organization called El Puente, which is a human rights institution with a mission to inspire and nurture leadership for peace and justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: It was founded in 1982 by immigrants of the Puerto Rican and Caribbean diaspora with the dream of reaching their countries in the future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: This dream became true with the establishment of El Puente Puerto Rico in 2013 and environmental and climate justice as a central axis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: This is precisely what enabled us to examine in detail the documents presented by the proponents of the Esencia project with our teams of lawyers and environmental scientists and prepare these comments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Resolution number 494, number 27, number 28, and number 372 are all measures that seek justice for Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Puerto Rico's colonial sorrows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Resolution 494 aimed at stopping Project Essencia correctly identifies many of the numerous issues raised by surrounding communities, scientific and environmental groups.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: El Puente Puerto Rico analyzed these documents submitted by the proponents of the Essencia project to the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Office of Management Permits, which revealed significant methodological, legal, and conceptual inconsistencies, raising serious doubts about the transparency and scientific rigor of the proposal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Essencia would be detrimental for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: For Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Essencia documents before OGP's evidence a series of negative impacts on species listed as vulnerable or threatened and on their critical

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: habitat with the project bordering the body, the body, the book.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Boquerin Wildlife Refuge, the Boquerin Forest, and the Lajas Valley Agricultural Reserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: It threatens ecosystems and species of high ecological value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Numerous vulnerable or endangered species have been identified in the areas to be impacted, as well as protected plants in the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Peñones de Melones and threatened marine species and corals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: There's a lot of more information regarding how a proyecto esencia will affect Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: I will submit my testimony, but I will say that El Puente and myself, we are in favor of the four resolutions presented today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Helen Colon
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Staff calls the next panel. Elba Montalvo, founder of the Committee for Hispanic Children and Families, testifies in support of all four resolutions. She discusses the impact of U.S. laws on Puerto Rican families and children.
chapters.title: Council Staff calls next panel; Elba Montalvo testifies

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Next we're going to have Dante Apuña, Davila Jimenez, Elba Montalvo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: Like a little girl in a big, at the principal's desk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: Good afternoon, buenas tardes, and thank you City Council for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: It's very important to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: My name is Elba Montalvo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: I am the founder and the former executive director.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: of the Committee for Hispanic Children and Families in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: I am also the former chair of the Puerto Rican Women's Foundation, Fundación de Mujeres en Puerto Rico, FNPR, an organization that I founded with activist women leaders from Puerto Rico

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: and the New York City Puerto Rican diaspora.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: FNPR was launched because, mindful of Puerto Rico's colonial status, we in the diaspora were searching for a way to help our sisters in Puerto Rico deal with the disastrous impact of Hurricane Maria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: It evolved into a philanthropic entity to address the deeply embedded societal issues, economic inequality, racism, and gender bias.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: I am giving testimony today as an individual.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: I was born in San Sebastian, Puerto Rico, raised in New York City, and for more than 30 years, I have supported services for children and families in Puerto Rico

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: through advocacy in Washington and by training Puerto Rican family judges around the implementation of legislation on adoption and domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: My work advocating for appropriate child welfare services for Puerto Rico has been necessary because the laws that are imposed on Puerto Rico by the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: Reflect the priorities and beliefs of the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: Rather than Puerto Rico's own cultural and family beliefs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: They are therefore not always in the best interest of Puerto Rican women and children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elba Montalvo
utterances.text: I support all four legislations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: stop Wall Street from profiting from Puerto Rico's debt crisis, end La Junta that has become our imperial master

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: and governs with impunity, and stop Project Esencia, as many of our brothers and sisters have said today,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It is a project that it built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm tired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Ay, carajo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It is a project that it built will have a devastating economic and ecological impact in the area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And repeal Act 22, it shields the wealthy from paying taxes and has allowed them to siphon off resources from working class Puerto Ricans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Every crisis and foundational problem that is confronted by the people of Puerto Rico is both connected to and magnified by its colonial status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I support the city council for its work to pass four bills that will help address some of the damage caused by Puerto Rico's colonial status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Council Member Aviles moves to a Zoom panel. Antonio Rosario, a proud Boricua with family in Cabo Rojo, testifies in support of Resolution 494. He describes the water and infrastructure challenges facing the island.
chapters.title: Alexa Aviles moves to Zoom panel; Antonio Rosario testifies

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Gracias, gracias.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Next we're going to move to a Zoom panel.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: We're going to have Antonio Rosario.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: We're going to resume in person.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: We are going to give opportunity for Antonio Rosario, Calvin, and Freddie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Gracias, Alexa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Can everybody hear me?

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Yes, we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Please start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: My name is Antonio Rosario.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I'm a proud 32-year teenster, a worker, a father, and proud Boricua.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: And today, I'm speaking not just as someone who cares about Puerto Rico, but someone who has family that comes from Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: My mother was born in Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I spent my summers there as a kid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Cabo Rojo is in some distant place on a map to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: It is a part of who I am.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: And now I bring my own children there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: We visit our families that are down there in Cabo Rojo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I used to run around La Santa Rita Residencial as a kid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: We call them caserios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: We visit our family.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: We walk the land.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: We see the beauty of the island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: And we also see the reality that the people living there face every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I've been there when the water has been shut off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I've been there when the electricity has gone out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: I've seen firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: What those things mean for our families who live there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: So when I hear about a massive development that could require more than 1.25 million, excuse my language, sorry, gallons of water every day, I don't hear the number.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: The statistic, I think about my familia, I think about the people who already live there, and I have to ask, how can we talk about building luxury resorts and golf courses and private

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: residences when the people who already call Cabo a home are still dealing with basic infrastructure challenges?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: That's why I'm here today to support Resolution 5494.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: The New York City Council's resolution recognizes Project Exacia for what it is, a proposed $2 billion luxury development covering more than 2,000 acres with hundreds of hotels, more than 1,000 residences, golf courses, private airport, and luxury amenities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: The resolution also raises concerns about water, wetlands, endangered species, archaeological sites, public beaches, and the impact of the surrounding communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: And these concerns aren't coming only from the people standing outside with protest signs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: The Puerto Rican Senate has been investigating the project.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: In recent hearings, government agencies have raised serious questions about infrastructure and water capacity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: The Puerto Rico Aqueducts and Sewer Authority has stated that existing Potencias filtration plant does not have the design capacity to supply the project and stimulate demand without additional infrastructure improvements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: That matters to me because I've seen the consequences of the inadequate water structure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: And I want the children of Puerto Rico and the working families are told to conserve water while luxury developments are guaranteed with resources they need.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Water is not a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Electricity is not a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Housing is not a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: A healthy environment is not a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: These are things that people deserve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: These are human rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: brings me to Resolution 2728.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: These resolutions speak a larger question on who determines Puerto Rico's future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Resolution 27 calls for the action against financial practices that allow outside financial interests to profit from Puerto Rico's debt crisis, while Resolution 28 calls on Congress to establish a date certain for ending the financial oversight and management board.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: For me, these issues are connected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Because whether we're talking about debt, development, land, water, and natural resources, we have to ask, who's Puerto Rico developed for?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Is it being developed for the people who live there?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Is it for the families who have their generations?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: For our children?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Being developed for ground one outside investors and extract the island, Puerto Rico cannot simply be treated as an investment opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Viva Puerto Rico, viva Puerto Rico libre.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Antonio Rosario
utterances.text: Esencia Canova, sorry.

chapters.summary: Calvin Yohannan, board member of Boricuas Unidos en la Diaspora, testifies in support of Resolutions 494, 27, and 28. He connects the Puerto Rican diaspora's history to the island's colonial status.
chapters.title: Calvin Yohannan testifies on resolutions

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Gracias, Tony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Calvin.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: My name is Calvin Yohanan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: I live in Brooklyn and I'm a board member of Boricuas Unidos en la Diaspora or BUDPR, a national organization advocating for Puerto Rico's sovereignty and independence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: I'm here today in support of Resolutions 494, 27, and 28.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: My mother is a New Yorker from the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Her parents raised on the island and like so many Puerto Rican families, ours came to New York through a migration shaped by colonialism, economic displacement, and limited opportunity in Puerto Rico.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: My abuelo drove subway cars and worked as the tower man for the MTA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Puerto Ricans did not just move to the city, they helped build it and quite literally kept it moving while carrying Puerto Rico with them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: The Puerto Rican diaspora in New York is not separate from Puerto Rico's colonial history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: In many ways, it is a product of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: That is why these resolutions matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Project Decencia, Abusive Debt Practices, and Unelected Fiscal Oversight and Management Board may seem like separate issues, but they reflect the same problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Puerto Ricans repeatedly having major decisions about their land, economy, and future made by institutions that are not accountable to them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Resolution 494 recognizes the threat of large-scale development that puts outside interests ahead of Puerto Rican communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Resolution 27 addresses harmful debt practices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: while Resolution 28 challenges an unelected fiscal board with extraordinary power over Puerto Rico's economy and public institutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: New York City should take a clear stand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Our families did not stop caring about Puerto Rico when they moved here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: On behalf of myself and as a member of Bud PR, I respectfully urge the council to pass resolutions 494, 27, and 28 and stand with Puerto Ricans demanding democratic control, dignity, and an end to colonial rule.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Calvin Yohannan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: Deputy Speaker Williams, Council Member Aviles, members of the City Council, buenas tardes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: I'm a senior director and researcher at New York Communities for Change, NYCC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: NYCC is a 20,000 member New York economic and social justice organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Since 2018 or so, I have worked with a coalition of other New York nonprofits on a Wall Street accountability campaign connected to the Puerto Rico debt crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Our work has led to a package of legislation that includes the reinstatement of charity, a law that stretches back a century that prevented creditors from abusing the court systems, and is one of the few legal protectionist countries in financial trouble had access to until 2004.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Buying the debt of a country in economic distress to extract profits by endlessly litigating should be and was illegal until 2004.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Debt relief organizations, the investor community, and government all agree this situation allows creditors of this category of debt to opportunistic debt to opportunistic debt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: take advantage of an anomaly in the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Our narrow change in this pre-existing law ameliorates the effects of leaving countries disproportionately vulnerable to exploitative creditors because they did not have the same protections others were eligible for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: And most people see as an egregious abuse of the judicial process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Nations default under New York law must also deal with the 9% interest of their debt, a number established in an era of much higher rates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: That payment starts right away and goes directly to the litigator until the judgment is arrived at, giving the litigious creditor a perverse incentive to prolong the situation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: This revised bill would also reduce this antiquated rate to a current and fair level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: And your communities are changing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: We are ultimately grateful to our members from the Puerto Rican diaspora who led the charge on this campaign because it is their experiences that has given us and gives us the motivation to persevere through years of challenges to arrive at this moment when we can see the light at the end of a long tunnel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: New York has the power to reinstate champion and give back a tool that creates stability for countries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: The New York bond market and holds vulture funds accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Your support of this legislation is appreciated and important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jose Gonzalez
utterances.text: Thank you again for your time and consideration on this matter.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Jose, for your testimony.

summary: Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries and International Relations held an oversight hearing on the research collections of NYC's public libraries at the Schomburg Center, plus four resolutions on Puerto Rico.
Library leaders from NYPL, Brooklyn Public Library, and Queens Public Library testified about their collections, funding needs, digitization efforts, and community engagement.

Public testimony included Puerto Rican community members, scholars, and activists supporting resolutions on ending the fiscal oversight board, repealing Act 22, stopping Project Esencia, and curbing predatory debt practices.
title: Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries and International Relations
topic: Oversight - Telling Our Stories: Examining the Research Collections of New York City’s Public Libraries
